obligations.behavior: Polar night only: cream light mode (bg #f5f0e6, ink #38362f) and slate dark mode, Auto following the host theme plus Light/Dark override; Lato for every role; the chart series palette re-validated with the dataviz validator for both modes before shipping; no theme picker
obligations.source_text: The fleet dashboard ships Polar night as its theme (cream light mode, slate dark mode, Auto follows the host theme); Geothermal, Kiln and Aurora remain in the locked reference only

obligations.behavior: ventunoq is chosen only for the exact compatible tokens arduino,monza or qcom,qcs8300; Spark, Thor and Orin detection results are unchanged
obligations.source_text: platforms.detect() recognises the VENTUNO Q from proc/device-tree/compatible (arduino,monza / qcom,qcs8300) and resolves a built-in 'ventunoq' profile; today detect() reads only device-tree/model ('Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. Monaco Monza addons', platforms.py:158-181) so this box falls to 'generic'

obligations.behavior: gpu-clock lock/unlock on a ventunoq box exits 1 with an unsupported-platform error and never invokes the root helper
obligations.source_text: heat-governor does not drive the GPU clock on the VENTUNO Q in this work: gpuclock gains an explicit unsupported-platform guard, because the shell helper's is_jetson() (gpuclock.py:109) would fall through to nvidia-smi -lgc, which does not exist here

obligations.behavior: while apply = false the cultureos daemon never pauses or CPU-caps a container and its state reports applying false
obligations.source_text: heat-governor is installed on cultureos (uv tool + user unit + config like the other four) so the VENTUNO Q is the fifth governed, observable box, running in dry-run (apply = false) until the declared VENTUNO Q limits are checked under load; today 'which heat-governor' is empty and the unit does not exist

obligations.behavior: BatchMode only; ConnectTimeout and a per-poll timeout bound every poll; one box failing or hanging never delays the others; the reader never changes a remote file or listen address
obligations.source_text: a fleet reader on cultureos polls all five boxes server-side: the four remote daemons through a persistent SSH connection per box (`ssh <box> curl 127.0.0.1:9476/state`, no change on any box) and cultureos locally; it tracks per-box ok/stale/unreachable on the reader's own clock, reusing pair.PeerLink's staleness logic, keeps a rolling buffer of the polled documents for trends, and never uses client.read's admit-on-unknown default

obligations.behavior: a daemon's tick interval is unchanged whether the fleet reader is running, slow or down
obligations.source_text: the fleet view is read-only and outside every daemon's control path: state schema 1 is unchanged (no renamed/removed fields, top-level level/admit/concurrency_factor/cpus keep their meaning, pair shown separately) and a dead box never delays any daemon tick

obligations.behavior: mesh overview, mesh status, mesh serve and mcp each take --json, keep results on stdout and errors on stderr with exit codes 0/1/2, and pass teken cli doctor --strict
obligations.source_text: a 'mesh' noun (overview, status [--json], serve) and a top-level 'mcp' verb are added through register(sub) in _build_parser with parser_class=type(p), ENTRIES in explain/catalog.py, the learn _TEXT/_as_json_payload lists and overview _VERBS, so teken cli doctor --strict and test_every_catalog_path_resolves stay green

obligations.behavior: stdout carries only JSON-RPC frames, all logging goes to stderr, and the tool list contains no tool that pauses, caps, applies or edits config
obligations.source_text: 'heat-governor mcp' speaks MCP over stdio with read-only tools (mesh status, one box's state, sense) and owns stdout for JSON-RPC framing: all logging goes to stderr via emit_diagnostic; it still accepts --json and 'mcp --help' returns

obligations.behavior: an invalid host entry fails config load with exit 1 and a hint; ssh is never spawned for it
obligations.source_text: the fleet reader validates every host in the fleet list as a plain hostname or IP (no leading '-', no spaces or shell metacharacters), passes '--' before the host and runs a fixed remote command, so a host entry can never become an ssh option such as -oProxyCommand

obligations.behavior: connections are reused across polls under a ControlPath in the reader's state dir and torn down when the reader exits
obligations.source_text: the reader manages its own persistent SSH connections (ControlMaster/ControlPersist with a ControlPath under its state dir), with BatchMode=yes, ConnectTimeout, ServerAliveInterval and a per-poll timeout, independent of the operator's ~/.ssh/config; today ~/.ssh/config sets only IdentityFile and a fresh poll measured 0.55 s

obligations.behavior: per-box buffer is bounded to 24 h of compact samples; memory does not grow past the bound over a week of polling
obligations.source_text: the reader's history buffer stores compact samples (time, hottest temperature, GPU temperature, level, admit factor) bounded to 24 h per box, not raw /state documents; probe: /state is 2-3 KB, so raw docs at a 2 s poll would be about 130 MB per box per day

obligations.behavior: every surface shows per-box last-poll time and transport errors distinctly from thermal level
obligations.source_text: mesh status, the MCP tools and the page report the reader's own health (when each box was last polled, reader uptime, transport errors) separately from each box's thermal state, so a dead reader never looks like five stale boxes
